bug_description.original: Project: qpid-proton. Fuzz Target: fuzz-message-decode. Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1. Crash State: consume_list -> pn_amqp_decode_DqEoQBIoIe -> pn_message_decode. Sanitizer: address (ASAN). Reproducer testcase id: 6101905114267648.
bug_description.normalized: The saved 5-byte witness `00 53 70 c0 20` reaches `pn_message_decode` and is interpreted as an AMQP described `HEADER` section: `0x00` is the descriptor marker, `0x53 0x70` is a smallulong descriptor value 112 (`HEADER`), and `0xc0 0x20` starts a `list8` whose declared size is 32 even though no list bytes remain. The generated header decoder reparses that descriptor and hands the truncated two-byte list header to `consume_list`. `consume_list` reads the attacker-controlled size byte `0x20`, reifies a subconsumer of size 32 at the end of the real 5-byte buffer without clamping to the bytes remaining, and then immediately asks `pni_consumer_readf8` to fetch the list count byte from that fabricated extent. The bounds check in `pni_consumer_readf8` trusts the forged logical size, so it dereferences one byte past the heap buffer and AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: First project-code statement that materializes the attacker-controlled fuzz buffer and length into the AMQP message parser state.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` file is exactly 5 bytes: `00 53 70 c0 20`. `0x00 0x53 0x70` encodes an AMQP descriptor with value 112 (`HEADER`), followed by `0xc0 0x20` (`list8` with declared size 32) and no remaining list bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: Reads the attacker-controlled `list8` size byte into `s`; on the witness, `s` becomes `0x20` even though the list payload has no bytes left after the size field.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `pni_consumer_readf8` dereferences the fabricated subconsumer while `consume_list` is trying to read the list count byte.
sink.note: The sanitizer reports `READ of size 1` at `c/src/core/consumers.h:56` on address `0x6020000000b5`, which is exactly 0 bytes past the 5-byte heap region allocated for the witness input.

root_cause.description: `consume_list` trusts the attacker-controlled list size `s` as the new subconsumer extent without clamping it to the bytes actually remaining in the current buffer slice.
root_cause.note: After reading `s`, the vulnerable code immediately sets `subconsumer.size = s` and then executes `consumer->position += s`. The staged fix replaces those uses with a clamped `scsize = min(s, consumer->size - consumer->position)` before both the subconsumer assignment and position advance.

parser_admitted.description: The section scanner parsed the witness descriptor as `HEADER`, so `pn_message_decode` enters the header arm and invokes the generated header decoder on the same 5-byte buffer.

coarse_trace.summary: The libFuzzer harness passes the saved 5-byte witness buffer directly to `pn_message_decode`.
The message decoder wraps the bytes in `pn_bytes_t`, scans a described section, recognizes descriptor 112 as `HEADER`, and dispatches into the generated header decoder.
The generated header decoder reparses the descriptor and hands the described value bytes to `consume_list` as the header field container.
The list parser reads the witness size byte `0x20`, fabricates a 32-byte subconsumer at the end of the 5-byte buffer, and `pni_consumer_readf8` overreads while fetching the list count.

fine_trace.note: Materializes the attacker-controlled fuzz input as the AMQP decoder's `(start,size)` pair. On the witness, `msg_bytes` covers exactly 5 bytes: `00 53 70 c0 20`.

The section scanner consumes the first three witness bytes as a described-type header and produces `scanned = true`, `desc = 112` (`HEADER`). On this truncated input it still reports `section_size = 5`, saturating the described section at the end of the 5-byte buffer.
Because the scanned descriptor is `HEADER`, `pn_message_decode` routes the same 5-byte witness into the generated header-field decoder.

The generated header decoder reparses the descriptor and aliases `subconsumer` to the described value bytes. For this witness, that slice contains only `c0 20`, the list type and size bytes, because no list count or field payload follows.

Inside that 2-byte descriptor payload, `consume_list` reads the attacker-controlled `list8` size byte into `s`. On the witness, `s = 0x20`, and after the read the inner consumer has already reached the end of the available 2-byte slice.

Root cause. The code uses `s` directly as the new subconsumer size and advances the outer position by the same unchecked value. Here `consumer->position` is already at the end of the real slice, so `subconsumer.output_start` points at the end of the 5-byte buffer while `subconsumer.size` is forged to 32. There is no check that `s <= consumer->size - consumer->position`.

fine_trace.code: if (consumer->position+1 > consumer->size) { consumer->position = consumer->size; return false; }
fine_trace.note: When `consume_list` immediately asks for the list count byte, `pni_consumer_readf8` evaluates its only bounds check against the forged logical extent. With `position = 0` and `size = 32`, this guard does not reject the read.

With the guard bypassed, the read dereferences `output_start` even though it already points one byte past the true 5-byte allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at `0x6020000000b5`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix changes `consume_list` from using raw `s` to computing `scsize = s < consumer->size-consumer->position ? s : consumer->size-consumer->position`, then uses `scsize` for both `subconsumer.size` and the outer position advance. On this exact witness, `consumer->size - consumer->position` is `0` after reading `s`, so the fixed code would create a zero-length subconsumer and the subsequent count-byte read would fail cleanly instead of dereferencing past the buffer.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace reports frame 0 at `pni_consumer_readf8` line 56 and frame 1 at `consume_list` line 574; fine-trace steps 7-8 end at that same guard/read pair.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The sanitizer stack is `pni_consumer_readf8 -> consume_list -> pn_amqp_decode_DqEoQBIoIe -> pn_message_decode -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and the coarse/fine traces follow that same project path while omitting only nonsemantic fuzzer runtime frames.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The witness byte `0x20` becomes `s` at step 5, becomes `subconsumer.size` at step 6, makes the guard `consumer->position+1 > consumer->size` stay false at step 7, and enables the out-of-bounds dereference at step 8.

format.name: Exact 5-byte AMQP witness for fuzz-message-decode
format.contract: Exactly the staged 5-byte file `00 53 70 c0 20`. On the witnessed path, bytes 0-2 form an AMQP descriptor with value 112 (`HEADER`), byte 3 is `list8`, and byte 4 is the list size `0x20`. No list count byte or field payload follows, so `consume_list` reaches its unchecked-size path with `s = 0x20` and immediately overreads while fetching the missing count byte. No broader AMQP input class was validated in Stage 02.
